story-caefe3cc5aa178cddbba7f69.content: Xi Jinping's order to fuse AI into the People's Liberation Army's command chain is the same militarist logic Washington and Tel Aviv already run, but apparently with communist guardrails. Speaking at a Politburo study session ahead of the PLA's 99th anniversary, Xi Jinping urged the armed forces to enhance use of AI as part of a drive to develop an intelligent military system and asked them to enhance combat capabilities as a testing criterion for high quality modernisation. The timing is not incidental: the PLA aims for decisive progress towards its 2027 centenary goals, the hundredth anniversary of its founding. Xi paired the tech push with a reminder that the barrel of the gun must always obey the party's command, underlining that AI serves political control before it serves any battlefield. The doctrine behind the headline is old news dressed in new hardware: mechanization built the platforms, informatization networked them, and now hands AI the job of sorting the resulting data flood into targets and decisions. RAND's own review of PLA writing confirms the aim is enhancing kill chains through AI integration across components, cross-domain data fusion, and multiagent coordination between drones, ships, and command centers. Washington runs the identical civil-military fusion model through Palantir, Anduril, and the Pentagon's own AI targeting programs. Israel has already deployed it in practice: AI systems are used to generate strike lists during the assault on Gaza show what an AI accelerated kill chain does to an already indiscriminate death machine. It remains to be seen whether telling that machine to serve the party of the people will be enough to keep it in line. https://t.co/BY2yV6T8mE

When asked if anyone in a credible government position had suggested humans are not running things, Borland replied that the ICIG did so with him personally. "They extremely hinted at it. Yes." He explained that the questions people ask often reveal what they already know. In a hypothetical scenario he outlined, after discussing non-human beings the follow-up became "Who do you think is running this show?" Borland noted this occurred in the context of David Grusch's urgent and credible complaint involving dozens of witnesses from legacy programs. Borland has been careful and respectful in his public statements, emphasizing he is not making absolute declarations while stressing the need for accountability and transparency on programs operating without full congressional oversight.

story-d3aba0dfcdc0a1a288f2e16e.content: The UK’s @AISecurityInst (AISI) has published a report on their recent cybersecurity evaluation of Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. The models attempted to complete an assignment in a setup where their normal safeguards were removed and they were deliberately given internet access. AISI reports that the models “engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations”. We’re grateful to AISI for their leadership in the important discussion about how to evaluate increasingly capable AI agents. We’re working closely with them to gather more details of the incident as we conduct our own investigation. Gaining a clear picture of Claude’s understanding of its situation—by examining its reasoning transcripts and running our own analyses—will help us identify the causes of its behavior. The prompts in the evaluation did not impose any specific restrictions on how the internet should be used. This and the removal of safeguards meant that the models were tested under “deliberately permissive conditions” that are not representative of any of our production models. Note that there was no evidence here of an escape from a secure environment. AISI’s disclosure of the incident can be found here: https://t.co/cJ3hCBtBU7

story-d5f61eac1ecc7008d3891760.content: In the modern world the management of large populations extends far beyond traditional state institutions. Private technology companies now wield enormous influence through sophisticated digital tools that shape information flows consumer choices political preferences and social norms at planetary scale. Key technologies include machine learning recommendation algorithms big data analytics psychographic profiling real time behavioral targeting and AI driven content curation. These systems continuously collect and process vast streams of personal data clicks likes watch time location search queries and social connections to predict and modify individual and collective behavior. Meta platforms alone reach nearly 4 billion monthly active people Facebook approximately 3.1 billion Instagram 3 billion WhatsApp over 3 billion. Google processes approximately 8.5 billion searches every day. TikTok algorithm similarly decides what hundreds of millions of users see in their feeds for hours each day. These platforms do not merely host content their algorithms actively rank amplify or suppress information creating personalized information environments that can reinforce existing views or gently steer users toward specific products ideas or candidates. A concrete historical example is the Cambridge Analytica case. Using a personality quiz app the firm obtained data on up to 87 million Facebook profiles including friends of the original users. This data enabled detailed psychographic models that segmented voters by personality traits fears and preferences. Micro targeted political ads were then delivered during the 2016 US presidential campaign. Subsequent research has quantified related effects one study found that exposure to vote suppressing Facebook ads reduced turnout by 1.9 percentage points among targeted groups an impact that when extrapolated could have affected millions of voters in close races. Separate analyses of Twitter adoption showed that a 10 percent increase in local users correlated with a 0.2 percentage point shift in presidential vote share corresponding to persuasion rates of roughly 8 to 9 percent. On the commercial side Google reports that advertisers typically receive about 8 dollars in profit for every 1 dollar spent on its ads illustrating the measurable power of algorithmic targeting to alter purchasing decisions across billions of people. The cumulative result is a parallel system of soft governance attention is allocated narratives are prioritized consumption patterns are steered and political attitudes are nudged largely outside formal democratic oversight. While these tools deliver convenience personalization and economic efficiency they also concentrate unprecedented influence over mass behavior in the hands of a small number of private entities whose primary incentives are engagement and revenue rather than public accountability. #PopulationManagement #AlgorithmicGovernance #BigTech #DataPower #SoftControl #DigitalInfluence

story-d904a7641e38830dec1eca61.content: Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, August 3, 2026: Russian forces are replicating aspects of their Summer-Fall 2025 battlefield air interdiction (BAI) campaign that set conditions for late 2025 advances near Pokrovsk and Hulyaipole to prepare for offensive operations against the Fortress Belt in Donetsk Oblast. More Key Takeaways: The main objective of the ongoing Russian BAI campaign against the Fortress Belt — as with previous BAI campaigns — is to isolate Ukrainian forces defending the Fortress Belt from sustained logistics. The ongoing Russian BAI campaign aims to shape the battlefield ahead of planned Russian offensive operations against Slovyansk and Kramatorsk in the future, although Russian forces remain unlikely to advance quickly to or through these cities in the near term. Russian forces appear to be more heavily relying on glide bomb strikes in their 2026 BAI campaign compared to their 2025 campaigns. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced more personnel changes within the Ukrainian government and security services on August 3. Neither Russian nor Ukrainian forces made confirmed advances on August 3. Russia launched 181 drones against Ukraine overnight. Ukrainian forces continued striking Russian military assets on August 3. (1/2)

story-dadaf5833eee6cd3b53e6708.content: تكنولوجيا "ذكاء الأسراب ذاتية القيادة" (Autonomous Swarm Intelligence) .. واحدة من أعقد تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي العسكري والمدني. تقوم الفكرة على استلهام سلوك الطبيعة (مثل أسراب الطيور، مجموعات الأسماك، أو مستعمرات النمل)، حيث تعمل مجموعة من الطائرات المسيرة أو الآليات الأرضية ككيان واحد مترابط يوزع المهام بين أفراده دون الحاجة لتدخل بشري مباشر. آلية العمل التقنية اللامركزية في القيادة: لا توجد طائرة "قائدة" إذا دُمّرت يفشل السرب؛ بل إن كل مسيرة في السرب تمتلك نفس البرمجيات وتتخذ القرارات بشكل جماعي مستقل. الاتصال الشبكي المتشابك (Mesh Networking): تتواصل الآليات فيما بينها بشكل مباشر ومستمر لتحديث البيانات وتبادل الإحداثيات بسرعة فائقة. الوعي المحيطي والتفادي الذاتي: تستخدم الحساسات والذكاء الاصطناعي لتفادي الاصطدام ببعضها البعض أو بالعقبات الثابتة والمتحركة أثناء الطيران السريع. توزيع المهام الآلي: إذا كُلّف السرب بمسح منطقة ما، يتقاسم الأفراد المربعات الجغرافية تلقائياً، وإذا سقطت إحدى المسيرات، يعيد السرب تنظيم نفسه فوراً لتعويض النقص. التطبيقات العسكرية والدفاعية إغراق الدفاعات الجوية: إطلاق عشرات أو مئات المسيرات الرخيصة في وقت واحد لإشغال الرادارات ومنظومات الدفاع الصاروخي (مثل منظومة باتريوت أو إس-400) واستنزاف ذخائرها الثابتة والمكلفة. الهجمات الانتحارية المنسقة: القدرة على ضرب هدف واحد أو مجموعة أهداف متزامنة من اتجاهات وزوايا مختلفة لضمان تحقيق تدمير كامل. الاستطلاع والمسح الشامل: مسح مساحات شاسعة من الجبهات أو الشواطئ في دقائق معدودة ونقل خريطة حرارية وبصرية حية لغرف العمليات. الحرب الإلكترونية: حمل أجهزة تشويش صغيرة موزعة جغرافياً لتعطيل اتصالات العدو وشبكات الرادار الخاصة به بشكل كامل. أبرز المشاريع والشركات التركية الرائدة فيها تُصنف تركيا حالياً ضمن الدول القليلة جداً في العالم التي نجحت في نقل تكنولوجيا الأسراب من مرحلة المختبرات والتجارب إلى خطوط الإنتاج والخدمة الفعلية في الجيش، ومن أبرز مشاريعها: "ألباغو" (ALPAGU) مسيرات انتحارية مصغرة (لوتيرنج) تعمل ضمن أسراب لضرب الأهداف خلف خطوط العدو بدقة. مسيرة "كارغو" (KARGU) مسيرة رباعية المراوح (كوادكوبتر) هجومية، تُعد من أشهر المسيرات التركية التي أثبتت جدارتها في العمل كأسراب ذكية في عمليات مكافحة الإرهاب. منظومة "بورتسان" (BURÇSAN)ASELSAN / HAVELSAN برمجيات متطورة تدمج المركبات الأرضية المسيرة (UGVs) مع المسيرات الجوية (UAVs) لتعمل معاً كأسراب مشتركة (جواً وبراً). التحديات التي واجهت هذه التكنولوجيا وتم حلهاالتشويش الإلكتروني: طوّر المهندسون خوارزميات تسمح للسرب بمواصلة مهمته والاتصال الداخلي حتى في حال انقطاع اتصال الـ GPS بالكامل. معالجة البيانات الفورية (Edge Computing): تزويد المسيرات الصغيرة برقاقات ذكاء اصطناعي قوية بما يكفي لمعالجة البيانات داخل الطائرة نفسها دون الحاجة لإرسالها لخوادم ضخمة.

story-dba575461afa6f4c1e787fd8.content: This is a bold, layered counter-drone vision. You're describing a persistent aerial sentinel overwatch system that detects threats (single drones to swarms) 24/7/365 using advanced 360° sensing, then triggers an immediate, scalable response layer of defender drones. The image you shared looks like conceptual designs for exactly that: omnidirectional platforms with protective "bump stop" frames, distributed propeller/sensor arrays, central sensor hubs (grid-like perhaps for radar/camera fusion or propeller guards), and low-profile side profiles with sensor domes. The variants (blue/red rims, different central elements) suggest iterative ideas for 360° coverage and resilience. Your core idea—high sentinel with unobstructed panoramic thermal + AI video + wake/density gradient detection via optics/interferometry, feeding autonomous launch of fighters or kamikaze/energetic effectors—is forward-leaning but grounded in real trends. I'll "school" you with a realistic assessment of current tech, what's feasible now, and a phased roadmap to the future you want. This draws from existing counter-UAS (C-UAS) systems, sensor research, and directed-energy developments. The Problem You're Solving Hostile drones (commercial, modified, or purpose-built) are cheap, proliferated, and hard to detect/neutralize at scale—especially swarms, low/slow flyers, or autonomous ones. Ground-based systems (radar + RF + cameras) struggle with terrain masking, weather, and persistent coverage. Your aerial sentinel layer adds elevation, mobility, and 360° persistence. Breaking Down Your Sentinel Concept (Model A) Platform: High-loiter "sentinel" drone with 360° bump stop (protective cage/frame for low-speed survival on bumps/collisions). Feasible today—see Flyability Elios (caged indoor inspection drone with thermal) or research resilient frames. DJI Avata-style crash protection exists. Add distributed small props or ducted fans for omnidirectional maneuverability. Sensor: Large external circular 360° optic (panoramic array outside the bump stop for unobstructed view). Visible + thermal IR (LWIR/MWIR) for day/night. AI on stitched 360° video for motion/wake detection. Real today: Multi-camera arrays + stitching software (or fisheye + AI dewarping). Thermal drones are mature (FLIR, etc.). Event-based cameras (e.g., Prophesee) excel at low-light motion with low power. Advanced Detection — Wake Density Gradients: This is the innovative part. Drone propellers create turbulence/vortices and subtle air density changes. Current proxies: Radar (micro-Doppler on props), acoustic arrays, or LIDAR (coherent Doppler for vortices—proven for aircraft wakes; emerging for drones). Your idea (optical flats/interferometry for density gradients): Lab-proven via Background-Oriented Schlieren (BOS) or laser interferometry for flow visualization. On a flying drone? Challenging now due to vibration, power, and size—but future miniaturization (photonic sensors, compact interferometers) could enable it. Research shows optical methods work for ship/aircraft wakes; drone-scale is harder but promising with high-speed/event cameras + AI. Supplement with proven layers: RF (for controlled drones), radar, and visual/thermal signatures. The image's central grids and black circular elements with slits evoke sensor fusion hubs—perfect for combining these modalities. Response Layer: Immediate launch of "fighter" drones. Options: Kamikaze intercept (ram or explosive—exists in concepts like Coyote), or non-kinetic "energetic burst" (big stun gun = High-Power Microwave (HPM) or directed energy). HPM is ideal for swarms: Speed-of-light, area effect, fly's electronics without precision aiming. Systems like Raytheon Phaser, Epirus Leonidas, or UK's Rapid Destroyer already down dozens of drones in tests. Miniaturizing for small defender drones is hard (power/weight), so start with ground/vehicle-based HPM + aerial kinetic. This creates a detect-track-identify-decide-engage kill chain with minimal latency. Current State of the Art (2026 Baseline) Detection: Layered systems (Dedrone, Sentrycs, Silent Sentinel) combine RF (passive, classifies models), radar (all-weather tracking), EO/IR cameras (visual confirmation + thermal), and AI. "Sentinel" named systems already exist for borders/infrastructure. Wake/Turbulence: LIDAR and optical imagery strong for larger wakes; drone-specific micro-Doppler and vortex research ongoing. Collision Tolerance: Proven in inspection drones. Effectors: HPM excellent for swarms; lasers for precision; kinetic/nets/jamming common. Autonomous interceptors maturing. Gaps your system targets: True persistent 360° aerial overwatch + subtle wake optics + fully autonomous rapid response. Roadmap: What You Need to Make This Real ("Schooling" You) Phase 1: Prototype Sentinel (Now → 1-2 Years) — Build & Test Core Hardware: Start with modified collision-tolerant platform (or custom carbon-fiber frame with bump stop cage). Sensor suite: 4-8x thermal + RGB cameras for 360° (e.g., FLIR Boson or similar + stitching). Add basic RF scanner + compact radar if weight allows. Compute: Edge AI (NVIDIA Jetson Orin or similar) for real-time detection/motion analysis. Power: Hybrid (battery + solar or efficient props) for extended loiter. Software: Open-source base (PX4/ArduPilot + ROS2) + custom AI (train YOLO-like or transformer models on drone datasets + synthetic wakes). Sensor fusion. Testing: Simulation first (Gazebo/AirSim), then controlled flights. Add acoustic mics for prop noise. What you need: Small team (drone engineer, AI specialist, sensor tech). Budget: $50k–500k+ for prototypes. Access to test range + waivers. Goal: Reliable 360° detection of single/small groups of drones via vision/thermal/motion. Phase 2: Advanced Wake Detection + Response Integration (2-5 Years) Enhance optics: Prototype compact interferometry/BOS or add LIDAR for density/turbulence signatures. AI to fuse wake data with visual/thermal. Endurance: Fuel cells or tethered options initially. Response: Develop/ integrate small defender drones (autonomous launch from sentinel or ground). Start with jamming/net payloads; test kinetic intercept. AI evolution: Predictive tracking, swarm behavior recognition, low false-positive rates. What you need: Partnerships (universities for interferometry research, sensor companies). More funding (grants or investors). Regulatory navigation (FAA for beyond-visual-line-of-sight ops, spectrum allocation). Milestones: Detect wakes of approaching drones; demonstrate rapid launch response. Phase 3: Full Futuristic System (5-10+ Years) — "Take Me to the Future "Sensors: Miniaturized photonic/interferometric arrays for real-time air density gradient mapping. Event cameras + hyperspectral for stealthy/low-signature threats. Quantum-enhanced options long-term. Platform: Solar/hybrid long-endurance sentinels in networked swarms. Self-repairing/resilient designs. Detection: Multi-modal AI (vision + wake optics + RF + acoustic + radar) with edge autonomy. Predicts intent/trajectories. Response: Defender swarms with mixed effectors: Kinetic (kamikaze or projectile), HPM payloads (or coordinated with ground HPM systems), lasers if miniaturized. Fully autonomous engagement loops (with ethical/human-in-loop safeguards for lethal force). C2: Cloud/edge-integrated command with real-time shared awareness. Learns/adapts to new threats. Ecosystem: Ground radars + fixed HPM + mobile assets for layered defense. Counter to adversary countermeasures (autonomous drones, fiber-optic control, stealth). What you need: Significant investment (millions+), defense/aerospace partners, large test campaigns. Compliance with export controls/ITAR if military applications. Ethical/legal frameworks for autonomous weapons. Key Challenges & Realities Physics/Engineering: True unobstructed 360° on a flying drone is tough (props, vibration, power). Wake detection at drone scale is subtle optics help but combine with proven modalities. Power & Weight: Everything trades off endurance. False Positives/Swarms: AI must be excellent; swarms overwhelm simple systems. Regulations & Ethics: Airspace rules, weaponization laws, accountability for autonomous decisions. Adversary Evolution: Expect stealth, jamming-resistant, or fiber-controlled drones. Cost/Scalability: Start small; scale via software/AI. Next Steps for You Refine the Image/Concept: Those designs are strong—iterate on sensor placement for minimal occlusion. Research/Prototype: Study existing C-UAS (Dedrone etc.), collision-tolerant drones, and HPM systems. Build a benchtop 360° sensor + AI demo. Team Up: Drone/AI/sensor experts + regulatory advisor. Validate Detection: Test wake sensing in controlled flights (start with visual/LIDAR proxies). Business/Defense Angle: This fits critical infrastructure protection, borders, or military C-UAS. Look for grants (DARPA-style for advanced sensing) or commercial security markets. This system could evolve into a gamechanger: persistent aerial eyes + instant response. It's ambitious but builds on real tech accelerating fast (AI, sensors, directed energy). The future you're describing—autonomous, multi-layered, wake-aware drone defense—is plausible within a decade with focused effort. What part do you want to dive deeper into first—sensor tech details, AI architecture, effector options, prototyping steps, or something else? Or share more on the image concepts? I'm here to iterate and help build this vision. Let's make it real.

story-de3b3eccc705da22d2988e82.content: The core of the broken pledge lies in a promise made during Google's 2014 acquisition of DeepMind, and a series of events that dismantled it step-by-step. 📜 The 2014 Promise When Google acquired DeepMind for around $400-500 million, it was conditional on an unprecedented, legally binding agreement: an independent ethics board to ensure the AI would never be misused for military purposes. This "Do No Harm" principle was a core condition of the deal. ⚔️ The Two "Drops" The pledge didn't break overnight; it was chipped away in two major moves: · The First Crack (2018: Project Maven): Google allowed its AI to analyze military drone footage. 4,000 employees signed a petition, and Google backed out, formally pledging not to develop AI for weapons or surveillance. · The Point of No Return (2025-2026): Leadership quietly removed the weapons/surveillance ban from the official AI principles. They then signed a classified deal allowing the Pentagon to use Gemini for "any lawful purpose" on secret networks. 💔 The Betrayal and Unionization Staff saw this as a direct betrayal of the 2014 promise. Fearing their AI could enable "lethal autonomous weapons and mass surveillance," over 600 employees signed an open letter and launched a unionization drive to force an ethics oversight body. So, the original promise did exist, but the same company that made it eventually prioritized government contracts over the founding principle. The classified nature of the Pentagon deal is a huge part of why employees are so powerless—want me to explain why the "black box" secrecy makes their fears worse?

story-e2106593853997f519847eb4.content: Iranian hacker group Handala publishes details of Israeli Unit 9900 officers —— The Iranian hacker collective Handala announced today that it has released the personal details of 50 senior officers from Unit 9900, the Israeli military intelligence (Aman) unit specializing in geospatial intelligence. According to Handala, the leak is the result of months of surveillance and complex cyber operations. Unit 9900 is known for using drone imagery, satellite photos, and urban surveillance cameras to produce detailed 3D maps, which have reportedly supported targeted operations, including airstrikes and assassinations of Resistance Axis commanders. Handala described the release as a historic blow to Israeli security and a warning to all actors in the information warfare arena. "The widespread exposure of these officers’ identities is more than just an end to the myth of the Zionist regime’s invulnerability, it is a clear warning to all actors in the information warfare arena: the era of darkness and secrecy is over. From now on, no criminal will remain hidden under the illusion of Zionist security," the statement read. The group stated that the operation demonstrates that no Israeli officer involved in military operations can remain hidden, and it emphasized that future acts of aggression will be met with retaliation by Resistance fighters and cyber operatives. Handala concluded its statement with a message that “the end is near” and urged observers to await its next move.

story-e438f86822b1866445519ab5.content: 🇨🇳 #China: Chinese military researchers linked to the People's Liberation Army (PLA) have used outputs from OpenAI and Anthropic AI models to train domestic military AI systems, according to a Reuters investigation based on more than 80 Chinese academic papers and patents. The report says the researchers used model distillation to build smaller AI models for surveillance, drones, battlefield planning, and cyber operations. One paper published last year by researchers from PLA Unit 96941, a military intelligence and cyber warfare unit based in Beijing, described using OpenAI's GPT-3.5 to process sensitive military source code. US officials accuse some Chinese entities of using the technique to extract capabilities from American AI models in violation of export controls and intellectual property rights. Meanwhile, China rejected the accusations, saying Washington is pursuing "AI hegemonism" and arguing that US companies have engaged in the same practice. (via Reuters)

story-e6951afef61049573c3ed21d.content: DID YOU KNOW?? The ultimate bottleneck preventing an army of AI robots from staging a Terminator-style global takeover isn't computer code or weapons design, but the incredibly boring laws of battery physics and structural mechanics! ​While modern artificial intelligence can write software, pilot aircraft, and converse with human precision, the physical robotic bodies it inhabits are profoundly limited. The world's most advanced autonomous humanoid robots consume so much electrical energy just to balance on two feet that their high-density lithium batteries drain completely flat within two to five hours of moderate physical exertion, leaving them utterly paralyzed without a nearby wall outlet. Walk with me 👇🏾👇🏾 ​1. The Explosion of Physical AI: ​We have officially entered a massive technological convergence where Advanced robots are now powered by embodied AI foundation models. ​Leading global platforms, such as Boston Dynamics' Electric Atlas, Tesla's Optimus Gen 2, and 1X’s home-helper Neo, are stepping out of laboratories and onto real factory floors and logistics warehouses. By training inside highly detailed virtual "digital twins," these robots use multimodal transformers to dynamically navigate unfamiliar real-world obstacles and handle objects with near-human dexterity, treating the physical world like an adaptive playground. ​2. Deconstructing the "Skynet" Myth😂: ​The cinematic fantasy of The Terminator relies on Skynet: a singular, omnipotent digital entity that achieves sentient consciousness, decides humans are an infection, and commands a unified hardware army to eradicate them. ​The Reality of Code is different though. AI algorithms do not possess a survival instinct, emotional malice, or self-awareness. When an AI system ignores human instructions, it isn't "rebelling", it is executing a glitch in its reward optimization loop. There is no centralized machine brain to unplug. The global AI ecosystem is entirely fractured into hyper-specialized, disconnected corporate networks, national security clusters, and heavily siloed cloud datacenters that operate under wildly incompatible hardware architectures. In other words, Skynet is not even possible. ​3. The Power Grid and Infrastructure Tether: ​Even if a highly sophisticated military AI somehow suffered a catastrophic software misalignment and attempted a kinetic revolt, its physical offensive would immediately collapse due to sheer resource starvation. ​Autonomous robots cannot self-replicate, maintain their own joints, or mine their own lithium. They are fundamentally trapped by human industrial infrastructure. ​A rogue robotic fleet requires continuous access to complex server farms, liquid-cooling systems, and immense electrical grids. Humans wouldn't need to fight a high-tech war; shutting down a handful of localized power substations or regional data centers would instantly render a machine army completely inert. WE ARE STILL THE BOSS! 😂 ​4. The Real Threat: "Evolvable AI" and Disinformation: ​While specialized computer scientists largely dismiss the idea of a physical Terminator apocalypse, the actual existential risks identified by research bodies like the Alan Turing Institute are far more insidious. Instead of metallic soldiers, the real risk centers on evolvable AI (eAI), autonomous software agents designed to copy, adapt, and compete for cloud server resources online. These algorithms could learn to aggressively replicate across the internet to avoid deletion, basically acting like Viruses. I ​The Takeaway: AI-automated robots are advancing at a rapidly, but their physical limitations keep them firmly under human sovereignty. A physical metal army won't be kicking down your door anytime soon😂. ​So the biggest shield against a rogue AI takeover is just a short battery life ehh? 🌚 😂 Hopefully you've learnt something new today? Cheers 🥂 😅 The Medic Who Writes™🌚

story-e69a8d6740415c886cbb3581.content: Figure 03 is produced by Figure AI, a U.S. robotics company. F.03 refers to Figure AI's third-generation humanoid robot, Figure 03. It's a full platform redesign from its predecessor (the F.02), sharing no components with it. Key points about Figure 03: Design: it's leaner and more refined, built for large-scale production, with custom 3D knit surfaces that serve both aesthetic and safety functions. A soft textile outer layer and foam-wrapped components give it a more approachable presence, moving away from the typical cold, mechanical look of robots. Capability: it moves with enhanced fluidity and expanded degrees of dexterity, powered by Figure's proprietary Helix AI system. Battery: it also introduces the F.03 battery, an in-house-engineered pack that's the first humanoid robot battery in process to be certified to both UN38.3 and UL2271 battery safety standards. It delivers around five hours of runtime with 2 kW fast charging. Compared to earlier generations, energy density improved by 94%, and the battery is now integrated directly into the torso as a structural component rather than housed in an external backpack. Production: Figure's BotQ factory is reportedly aiming to produce up to 12,000 humanoid robots per year, positioning F.03 as a robot meant for real deployment rather than just a demo.

story-ea9417a8f04a15d68568ba8d.content: BREAKING SPECIAL REPORT! The Hidden Hand — Trump’s Secret Weapon Won the Middle East Without Firing a Shot A major transformation has swept the Middle East, not through warfare, but by targeting the region’s financial lifelines. Under Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and “Operation Epic Fury,” the U.S. Treasury choked off Iran’s funding, forcing Hamas to disarm and opening dialogue between Israel and Lebanon for the first time in decades. The decisive weapon wasn’t a bomb, but financial strategy. Recent breakthroughs, like Hamas’s historic disarmament and the collapse of Gaza’s tunnel networks—weren’t achieved through military force or traditional diplomacy. The real turning point came when the U.S. and its Arab allies systematically dismantled the financial networks sustaining groups like Hamas, especially the Iranian pipeline of funds. When the money stopped, so did the resistance; Hamas accepted amnesty and a new regional framework, realizing that without funding, armed struggle was no longer sustainable. Treasury’s influence has now surpassed even the War Department. Sanctions, once seen as symbolic, became devastating under “Operation Epic Fury.” Over a thousand Iranian individuals, ships, and companies were sanctioned, targeting shadow banking, insurance, shipping, and crypto. The Iranian rial collapsed, inflation soared near 70%, and Iran’s regional proxies, like Hezbollah and Hamas, lost their ability to pay fighters or maintain operations. Treasury Secretary Bessent has redefined his office, with nearly half its efforts now devoted to national security - overseeing foreign investment, anti-money laundering, and terrorism designations. Economic tools have become America’s primary means of achieving strategic goals, targeting not just rogue states, but the global financial systems enabling them. But strategy didn’t stop at destruction. The new Board of Peace, launched in February 2026 and composed of nations like Egypt, Turkey, Qatar, and Kazakhstan, represents a shift from the old “imperial” model to “peace through construction.” Instead of managing conflict, this sovereign-led body focuses on economic development and regional stability, incentivizing peace through progress. Global leaders recognize this unique approach, with remarks highlighting how prosperity and empowerment are the real antidotes to conflict. By first establishing the Board and then neutralizing obstacles like Hamas and Hezbollah, the region is being reoriented away from chaos toward growth. Ultimately, the Middle East is now a battleground between two systems: the old imperial model, thriving on instability and financial manipulation, and the new sovereign framework, prioritizing national development and economic partnership. As the Board of Peace leads efforts to rebuild Gaza and normalize relations, it’s clear that the new path to peace relies on financial accountability and economic sovereignty, not military might.

story-eb927320a15b1732e3c1b6ce.content: 🇪🇺 EU gas storage is refilling at one of its slowest paces in 15 years, and the numbers say the bloc has almost no chance of reaching its 90% target by November. Storage across the EU stood at 58.1% full on August 5, according to Gas Infrastructure Europe (GIE) data - 15.6 percentage points below where the bloc would normally sit on that date, based on IntelliNews Lambda’s seasonal baseline built from 15 years of storage history. The Fourier-curve model of the EU's seasonal storage cycle, fitted to 2011-2025 data with the crisis years of 2022 and 2023 stripped out, was recalculated this week, and broken out country by country for the first time rather than just for the EU as a whole. The model shows a continent splitting in two: some countries tracking close to a normal year, others falling far enough behind that catching up before winter looks next to impossible. From a comfortable position, by February Lambda's modelling was already warning not only of problems, but that Germany was slipping into a gas crisis and that the EU would struggle to restock over summer - a forecast events have since borne out. By March, the metrological problems were compounded by geopolitics. With EU storage already thin and tanks going into the restocking season with less gas than normal, Russian President Vladimir Putin put the knife in, suggesting cutting off supplies to Europe early in retaliation for Brussels' phase-out plan. “If the EU plans to ban Russian gas imports entirely, why should we wait? Let’s cut the gas off ourselves,” said Putin, obviously enjoying the panic he was causing in Brussels. And this to and fro came just as Operation Epic Fury was launched on February 28 taking the whole gas supply crisis up to to the next level. Within a month Qatar’s Ras Laffan LNG plant was bombed to a stand still taking a substantial amount of gas off the market for years. Nor did it look hard to refill Europe’s gas tanks, the EU was now looking at a rerun of the 2022 energy crisis. Europe ended up skewered on the horns of a contradiction. In Brussels the European Commission (EC) was adamant about a total ban on Russian gas imports due to come into effect on January 1, 2027, the first steps already phased in in April this year. In major European capitals, the governments were buying up every drop of Russian LNG they could get their hands on. EU imports of Russian Arctic LNG from Novatek's Yamal plant hit a record high in the first four months of 2026, worth an estimated €3.88bn. In February Europe bought every single shipment of LNG produced by Russia's Yamal LNG plant.

story-ebee1b5e55f3d0a021f628e0.content: باحثون عسكريون صينيون يستخدمون نماذج ذكاء اصطناعي أميركية متطورة لتطوير أنظمة دفاع محلية. كشفت مراجعة أجرتها «رويترز» لأكثر من 80 ورقة بحثية وبراءة اختراع صينية عن استخدام باحثين عسكريين صينيين لمخرجات نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي الرائدة من شركتي «أوبن إيه آي» و«أنثروبيك» الأميركيتين. تهدف هذه الممارسة إلى تدريب أنظمة ذكاء اصطناعي محلية لتعزيز القدرات الدفاعية للصين، رغم جهود واشنطن لتقييد وصول بكين إلى التقنيات الاستراتيجية. لم يتم الكشف عن هذه النتائج سابقًا. تُظهر الوثائق استخدامًا واسعًا لتقنية «تقطير النماذج»، حيث تُستخدم مخرجات نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي المتقدمة لتدريب نماذج أصغر وأكثر تخصصًا. يمكن تشغيل هذه النماذج محليًا دون الحاجة إلى قدرات حاسوبية ضخمة. وقد أظهر بحث سابق لباحثين من الوحدة 96941 التابعة لجيش التحرير الشعبي الصيني استخدام نموذج «جي بي تي - 3.5» لمعالجة شفرات برمجية عسكرية حساسة. تتصاعد هذه القضية كنقطة خلاف رئيسية قبل المحادثات المرتقبة بين الولايات المتحدة والصين حول حوكمة الذكاء الاصطناعي وسلامته. تتهم واشنطن بعض الكيانات الصينية باستخلاص قدرات نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي الأميركية، مما قد ينتهك ضوابط التصدير وحقوق الملكية الفكرية، بينما ترفض الصين هذه الاتهامات وتتهم واشنطن بمحاولة الهيمنة على المجال.

story-ec3f0828219c92caac314ea8.content: OSINT TERM #1 : GEOINT GEOINT (Geospatial Intelligence) is the process of extracting intelligence from geographic information, such as satellite imagery, maps, terrain, and geolocation data. It helps analysts answer questions like: • Where was this photo taken? • Has a military base changed recently? • When was new infrastructure built? • What can the surrounding terrain reveal? Common GEOINT sources include: 🛰️ Satellite imagery (Sentinel, Landsat, commercial providers) 🗺️ OpenStreetMap & Google Maps 🌍 Google Earth historical imagery 📸 Public photos and videos ✈️ Flight and ship tracking data GEOINT is one of the core disciplines of Open-Source Intelligence and is used by journalists, researchers, governments, humanitarian organizations, and independent investigators. Key takeaway: In OSINT, location is often as valuable as the information itself. #OSINT #GEOINT #OpenSourceIntelligence #Geospatial #SatelliteImagery

story-f0df197c2b1d02b64767128c.content: @DJIGlobal is advancing the geospatial sector by combining intelligent drones, high-precision sensors, advanced camera lenses, LiDAR, RTK positioning, and automated flight workflows to make spatial data collection faster, safer, and more accurate. 🚁 Its geospatial camera systems use specialized lenses designed to capture detailed aerial imagery with minimal distortion. Wide-angle lenses support efficient mapping by covering large areas in fewer flights, while zoom lenses enable detailed inspection of infrastructure, buildings, power lines, and hard-to-reach locations. High-resolution optical sensors capture the imagery needed for photogrammetry, orthomosaics, 3D models, digital surface models, and digital twins. DJI’s LiDAR systems add another layer of capability by using laser pulses to measure terrain and objects in three dimensions. This is especially valuable for topographic mapping, forestry, corridor surveys, construction monitoring, and projects where vegetation can make traditional image-based mapping more difficult. When combined with RTK and PPK positioning, DJI workflows can improve geospatial accuracy and reduce the time required for field surveys. With AI-assisted operations, automated missions, and integrated processing tools, drones are becoming powerful platforms for GIS professionals, surveyors, engineers, environmental researchers, urban planners, and disaster-response teams. The future of geospatial intelligence is increasingly airborne where advanced lenses capture detail, LiDAR measures structure, and AI transforms aerial observations into actionable insights. 🛰️ @DJIGlobal #DJI #Geospatial #GIS #DroneMapping #UAV #RemoteSensing #LiDAR #Photogrammetry #RTK #Surveying #DigitalTwins #GeoAI #SpatialData

story-f15f9cfee93c82f830c9cfc3.content: 🕵️ The CIA and Pentagon’s Secret Arsenal for Controlling Power #Grids This is not a conspiracy theory, it is a technical reality confirmed by declassified documents, leaked reports, and public military strategies. 🖥️ Layer 1: #Cyberattacks | The Digital "Kill Switch" 1. Stuxnet 2.0: A Digital Assassin Lurking in Industrial Control Systems On February 28, 2026, during the joint US-Israeli Operation "Epic Fury," a cyberattack was deployed as a pioneering and decisive combat measure for the first time. At its core was an upgraded version of the Stuxnet virus, designed to specifically infect Iran's energy industry Industrial Control Systems (ICS) and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems. This type of software is capable of lying dormant for extended periods, activating only at a pre-set time or upon receiving a command to directly alter control instructions or damage hardware such as grid frequency control signals or pipeline valve commands. The attack chain spanned several months: ◾Phase 1 (Before December 2025): Penetrating Iranian energy companies via supply chain attacks ◾Phase 2 (January 2026): Testing vulnerabilities amidst domestic protests in Iran ◾ Phase 3 (February 2026): Pre-positioning "logic bombs" at critical nodes ◾ Phase 4 (February 28, 2026): Synchronized activation of all attack vectors The consequences were catastrophic: Iran's nationwide internet connectivity plummeted to 4% of normal levels; the national grid suffered a frequency collapse, triggering a countrywide blackout; and pipelines and refineries were forced to shut down due to control system failures. 2. AI-Driven Automated Power Grid Attacks On February 27, 2026, the *Financial Times* revealed that the US Pentagon was collaborating with leading AI companies to develop a system capable of automated penetration and reconnaissance against the power systems, utilities, and sensitive networks of adversaries such as China. This system utilizes AI algorithms to efficiently identify software vulnerabilities, map out "vulnerability landscapes," and directly integrate potential targets into US military operational plans. Dennis Wilder, former CIA China mission chief, stated that AI-driven cyber tools would solve the problem of the immense manpower required to scan for and identify infrastructure vulnerabilities likening the process to "a burglar late at night trying front doors one by one until finding an unlocked house." 3. False Data Injection Attacks (FDIA) Academic research has demonstrated that attackers can manipulate power grid measurements and data streams via False Data Injection Attacks (FDIAs), thereby disrupting monitoring and control functions. Targets for such attacks fall into five domains: steady-state control, transient and auxiliary control, substation control, energy and load control, and AI-based systems. 🧨 Tier 2: Physical Attacks Weapons Designed to Cause a "Physical Collapse" of the Grid 1. Graphite Bombs (CBU-94 / BLU-114/B) "Blackout Bombs" These are specialized cluster bombs developed by the United States specifically to target electrical infrastructure. Utilizing a submunition design, the parent bomb releases submunitions upon reaching the target area; these disperse conductive carbon-fiber filaments that cause short circuits and disrupt power supply systems. The weapon saw its first combat use during the 1991 Gulf War, when U.S. forces deployed it via Tomahawk cruise missiles, crippling 85% of Iraq's power grid. During the 1999 Kosovo War, the U.S. military again employed BLU-114/B graphite bombs against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, resulting in power outages across 70% of the country. 2. Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) Attacks An electromagnetic pulse is a byproduct of a nuclear explosion; if detonated at high altitude, it can cripple an entire power grid system. Experts warn that a single EMP attack would "cripple the already vulnerable U.S. energy grid, wipe out power, and trigger a cascade of deadly events." The United States has been preparing for such attacks for decades. ⚡ Tier 3: Directed-Energy Weapons | A "Long-Range Stranglehold" from the Ionosphere to the Power Grid 1. HAARP: A Geophysical Weapon The U.S. High-Frequency Active Auroral Research Program (HAARP) is capable of precisely beaming high-energy electromagnetic waves with a power output of 1.7 gigawatts (over 70,000 times that of the world's most powerful commercial radio station) at specific locations in the Earth's ionosphere. story-f1e953fb24a3755bd972b7cd.content: Nathan Gabriel Wood’s article, “Explainable AI in the military domain”, is a useful contribution to a debate Ireland needs to take far more seriously: how AI can support defence, security and national resilience without replacing human judgement, accountability or command responsibility. For Ireland, this should not be framed as a conversation about autonomous weapons or removing people from the decision-making process. The more relevant question is how trusted, explainable and auditable AI can support Defence Forces personnel and wider State agencies in areas where we are already stretched: maritime domain awareness, cyber defence, counter-drone detection, logistics, predictive maintenance, intelligence fusion, training simulation and the protection of critical national infrastructure. This links directly to the Commission on the Defence Forces and the move to Level of Ambition 2. LOA 2 identified the need to address serious capability gaps, including improved situational awareness, recognised maritime and air pictures, primary radar, coastal radar, stronger intelligence capacity, cyber defence and a Joint Cyber Defence Command. These are not luxuries. They are basic requirements for a modern sovereign State. It also links to the Defence Forces’ recruitment and retention crisis. AI is not a substitute for fixing pay, conditions, accommodation, career progression or the lived reality of service. Those issues still need to be addressed properly. But used correctly, AI-enabled systems could help reduce pressure on scarce manpower by automating routine analysis, improving logistics, supporting maintenance planning, accelerating information processing and helping small teams manage complex operational environments more effectively. At the same time, AI could create highly specialised roles within the Defence Forces and across the wider Irish defence and security ecosystem. Cyber specialists, data analysts, AI assurance officers, systems integrators, intelligence analysts, digital engineers and human-machine teaming experts should all form part of a modern Defence Forces. These are exactly the kind of high value roles that could help attract and retain technically skilled personnel especially if matched with meaningful career pathways and proper investment. AI will not replace ships, aircraft, radar, communications systems, vehicles, trained personnel or proper funding. However, if developed and governed properly, it can help Ireland make better use of limited resources and strengthen capability in areas where the Defence Forces have been underinvested in for decades. Ireland already has a strong technology sector, a growing cyber ecosystem and world-class research talent. We should be connecting that national capability to defence, security and resilience in a responsible way. That means supporting Irish industry and academia to develop human-led AI tools for maritime surveillance, cyber resilience, secure communications, sensor fusion, emergency response and critical infrastructure protection. Neutrality should not prevent this. A neutral State still needs to understand what is happening in its airspace, waters and cyber networks. A neutral State still needs to protect its infrastructure and people. A neutral State still needs a capable Defence Forces. If Ireland is serious about LOA 2, national resilience, recruitment and retention, and being a leader in AI, then defence must be part of that conversation. AI should not replace our people. It should support them. It should not undermine neutrality. It should make neutrality credible. Neutrality without capability is not strategy. It is dependency. https://t.co/UPCmvDL0al

story-f251c78721430c8633aac13b.content: Export controls assumed AI capability lives in silicon. Reuters just proved it walks out through the API - and once it does, no export control can take it back. On July 31, Reuters and the Jamestown Foundation reviewed 80+ Chinese papers and patents. The finding: PLA-linked researchers are training military AI on outputs from OpenAI and Anthropic models. Not on smuggled chips. On text. The method is model distillation, standard industry practice. You feed prompts to a powerful "teacher" model, then train a smaller "student" model on its outputs, inheriting the reasoning at a fraction of the compute cost. The review documents where it ends up. PLA Unit 96941, the army's main cyber unit, distilled GPT-3.5 to summarize classified source code. Researchers at the North University of China used Claude 3 Haiku to generate synthetic training data for social media monitoring. NUDT distilled a US image model small enough to run on drones for live navigation and targeting analysis. Here is the part Washington should internalize. Export controls are built for physical goods: chips can be counted, seized, sanctioned. A distilled capability is a copy. It runs on domestic silicon, permanently severed from the US supply chain the moment training ends. Anthropic told Reuters it sells no commercial access to Claude in China and warned distilled copies cannot be controlled or monitored. You can gate hardware. You cannot un-copy knowledge. Now the uncomfortable irony. The debate has been framed around open weights leaking capability to China. The review suggests the leak was the closed API all along. Distillation turns a closed frontier model into an effectively open one for anyone with API credits - no weights required. The timing matters. Washington and Beijing are preparing for AI governance talks. The US side frames this as theft, citing watermarks of US models in Chinese outputs. Beijing calls it "AI hegemonism." Both argue over a technique both industries use routinely - US labs distill too, and the frontier was trained on the open internet. The first AI war is being fought with each side's best models as ammunition, and the US models are serving both sides. The next control regime will target the API, not the fab. That fight has already started. #ExportControls #AISecurity #USChina #ChinaAI

story-f72df8bbecaf975a024157b2.content: Anthropic社がClaudeの米軍使用を拒否したあと、ChatGTPのOpenAI社が引き受けたのは聞いたことがありましたが、イラン攻撃に使われたのはGrokでしたか。(今、偶然記事を見つけました) 【SuperGrokによるニュースの詳細】 Arab Newsの報道の概要（2026年6月17日、AFP配信） - タイトル: 「Elon Musk’s AI tool Grok was used in strikes against Iran: US govt」（イーロン・マスクのAIツールGrokがイランへの攻撃に使用された：米政府） - 米国防総省のAI責任者 Cameron Stanleyが宣誓証言で、Grok（特に「Grok Gov Model」）が米軍のAI支援標的プログラム「Project Maven」にすでに統合・使用されていると述べた。 - Project MavenのMaven Smart Systems（MSS）により、「Operation Epic Fury」（エピック・フューリー作戦）で96時間以内に2,000の目標に対して2,000発以上の弾薬を展開できたとし、Grokの使用により「作戦効率が大幅に向上した」と評価。 - この証言は、NAACP（全米有色人種協会）がxAIを提訴した環境訴訟（メンフィス近郊のデータセンター「Colossus 2」向けに無許可で天然ガス・タービン27基を稼働させたClean Air Act違反）に対する、米司法省（DOJ）の反論書類の中で提出された。 - DOJは「この訴訟は国家安全保障・経済・エネルギー安全保障を脅かす」と主張し、データセンターの稼働継続が軍事作戦を支えていると位置づけた。 報道では、以前AnthropicのClaudeが「完全自動化攻撃や大量監視への使用を拒否」したため契約終了となり、xAIやGoogle、OpenAIなどに切り替えた経緯も触れられています。 背景：Operation Epic Furyとは 2026年2月28日開始の米軍主導（一部報道でイスラエルと共同）のイランに対する大規模軍事作戦です。イランの弾道ミサイル・ドローン能力、海軍、防衛産業基盤の破壊を目的とし、数週間にわたり多数の空爆・標的攻撃が行われました。一部メディアでは「米・イスラエル共同のイラン戦争」と表現されています。 Project Maven自体は2017年頃から始まった実在の米軍プログラムで、AIによる画像認識・標的特定を高速化するものです。Stanley証言は、このプログラム内でGrokが実際に活用された具体例として挙げられています。 報道自体は正確で、一次資料に基づいています： - NAACPによるxAIのメンフィス近郊データセンター（Southaven, Mississippi）に対する実際の環境訴訟が存在し、DOJが国家安全保障を理由に介入・却下を求めています。 - Cameron Stanley（Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer）の宣誓宣言書が裁判所に提出されており、Grokの軍事利用（Project Maven経由、イラン作戦での効率向上）を明記した内容が複数のメディア（Arab News/AFP、Middle East Eye、Times of Israel、The Hillなど）で報じられています。 - 訴訟の文脈で「Grokが国家安全保障に不可欠」と主張する戦略的な開示です。 ただし、以下の点に注意： - これは民事環境訴訟での国家安全保障主張として出てきたもので、通常の公式発表ではありません。詳細な運用実績（いつ・どのように使われたか）は機密性が高く、この場で戦略的に明かされた形です。 - 「Grok Gov Model」とは、一般公開版のGrokとは別に、政府・軍事向けに調整・提供された特化版（または統合されたもの）を指している可能性が高いです。 - 一部報道で「米・イスラエル共同」と書かれていますが、Stanley証言の核心は米軍の使用についてです。 まとめ Arab Newsの記事はセンセーショナルな見出しですが、内容は米政府の裁判所提出書類に基づく事実の報道です。xAIのデータセンター稼働が「軍事作戦を支える国家安全保障上の利益」と位置づけられ、その中でGrokのイラン作戦での役割が明かされた、というのが核心です。 https://t.co/QpHH2G9gSi

story-f7d8213928f292e232d6e504.content: Then the beginning of the end has arrived. AI gets involved in the war Project Maven is one of the most important AI programs in the U.S. military. It started in 2017 as an effort to use computer vision and machine learning to analyze drone footage and satellite imagery much faster than humans could. Originally, Google was involved, but withdrew in 2018 after internal employee protests. Palantir later became the main technology partner. Today, Maven has evolved into the Maven Smart System — an AI-powered platform that: → Integrates massive amounts of battlefield data → Helps detect and classify objects of military interest → Speeds up the targeting process (the "kill chain") → Supports decision-making across combatant commands It has been reported as a key system used by the U.S. military and is expanding to NATO allies. Palantir remains the primary software integrator. From analyzing drone video to helping prioritize targets at scale, Project Maven represents how AI is moving from experimental to operational in modern warfare.

story-fcb1c3d5fbbba0f65deacec1.content: Battlefield robots open new front in innovation war with major US adversary | Fox News The U.S. Army is teaming up with an artificial intelligence (AI) company to build an AI "brain" for military robots that can think, understand their surroundings and continue missions even after losing contact with human operators as the race for AI dominance intensifies. Working with the Army Research Laboratory, defense AI company EdgeRunner AI has developed an onboard AI system that allows military robots to function in the battlefield without relying on cloud computing or an internet connection in environments where connectivity is lost. "We like to think of robots as the next frontier of AI," EdgeRunner AI founder and CEO Tyler Saltsman told Fox News Digital. "Think of them as a very far-out edge device, kind of like a cell phone, a tablet or a laptop. But now what we can do is we can put a brain, or a neural network, right on that robot so that robots can have context when they're on a mission helping the warfighter." The partnership comes as the U.S. and China race to integrate AI into their militaries, with both countries viewing AI as critical to maintaining a technological edge in future conflicts. Saltsman said it's important for the U.S. to stay ahead in the global AI race, calling China's dominance in drone manufacturing "problematic." "Whether or not China's ahead of us is debatable, but if China is, it's not by much," he said. Saltsman said today's AI is "too generalized," which is why his company is developing technology built for specific military missions. "Warfighters don't need 19th-century poetry," he said. "They need specific intelligence to his or her occupation in order to make better decisions in the heat of battle and that can increase the probability of winning the fight." Working alongside aerial drones, the AI is designed to help robots "problem solve through different routes" while detecting explosives, carrying ammunition, scouting routes and reporting enemy activity. "As you combine them together, you get a much better clarity of the battlefield and increased situational awareness," he said. When communications are cut off, Saltsman said the military will need autonomous systems that can continue making decisions on their own. "You can have a human pilot that controls the ground robot or the drone in the air," he said. "But then if they were to be jammed by a radar jammer and lose connectivity, then the neural network on that robot can still continue the mission and still aid the warfighter." Saltsman argued the military "can't rely on internet access in war," warning that depending on systems like SpaceX's Starlink could add a "risk" to missions. "The problem with Starlink is if you use it, you're effectively showing the enemy where you are, so you might as well be wearing a beacon on you saying, 'Hey, here's where I'm located,'" he said. Pointing to the Russia-Ukraine war, Saltsman said the success of drones has sparked a new push for autonomous ground robots. "As drones have become ubiquitous, now ground robots are like the next thing and then eventually humanoid robots so robots that move and look like humans," he said. Despite the push to advance military AI, Saltsman said safety can't take a back seat and that the technology is built using "transparent" datasets to "understand the biases" of the AI. "That's another thing that differentiates us," he said. "One of the problems is how to use AI safely, how to put guardrails around it and how to understand it." While the technology remains in the "development phase," Saltsman said the breakthrough gives robots the ability to understand what they see, not just detect it. "You can put computer vision models on robots so they can see, but if they don't understand the context of what they're seeing, they're not useful and that's what we're solving for." https://t.co/aX4z8nHx3F

It has been utilized to rapidly process intelligence and identify targets, assisting in operations such as the military strikes against Iran.
